register.labelZh: SIT 片語動詞的實際用途
register.summaryZh: sit around 表示無所事事地消磨時間;sit by 的意思更嚴重,表示眼看不好的事情發生,卻沒有採取行動。；sit in on a meeting 表示以旁聽者身分出席;sit in for somebody 表示暫代某人;sit on acommittee 則表示擔任委員會成員。；當某人選擇不參加或被迫錯過比賽、舞蹈、旅程或其他活動時,可以使用 sit something out。；sit back、sit somebody down 和 sit somebody up 分別描述三種不同的動作或坐姿。
register.summaryEn: Sit around means spending time doing very little. Sit by is more serious: it means failing to act while something wrong is happening. Sit in on a meeting means attending as an observer. Sit in for somebody means replacing that person. Sit on a committee means being one of its members. Sit something out is useful when someone chooses or has to miss a game, dance, trip or other activity. Sit back, sit somebody down and sit somebody up describe three different movements or sitting positions.

fixedVariable.variableZh: 保留原句中的人物、事物、時間和意思。；先學習核心表達。其他字詞可以補充資料,但不一定是固定表達的一部分。例如,sit by 是核心表達;and watch 和 while something happens 則解釋當時發生了甚麼事。；留意以下重要分別:● We sat out after dinner.我們晚飯後坐在室外。● I sat the game out.我沒有參加那場比賽。● She sat him down.她讓他坐下。● She sat him up.她扶他從躺着或靠着的姿勢坐起來。
fixedVariable.variableEn: Keep the same people, things, time and meaning. Learn the core expression first. Other words may add information, but they are not always fixed parts of the expression. For example: ● sit by ● sit by and watch ● sit by while something happens The core expression is sit by. And watch and while something happens explain what the person allowed to happen. Notice these important differences: ● We sat out after dinner. We sat outside. ● I sat the game out. I did not take part in the game. ● She sat him down. She made him sit. ● She sat him up. She helped him move from lying or leaning to a sitting position.
